title: Seniority & Career Level
finding: Your profile currently reads as entry-level for Laboratory Technician: you have 6.4 years of work history, but it is in retail (Bunnings/Coles), with no direct clinical lab experience yet. Your degree is relevant (Bachelor of Biomedical Science, 2023), but your own cover-letter line "I don't have any lab experience outside of uni" reinforces a junior positioning.
examples: "I don't have any lab experience outside of uni"
Retail-only employment history across Bunnings and Coles
recommendation: Confirm a Junior/Graduate framing, then position your application around readiness, trainability, procedural accuracy, and transferable reliability rather than trying to imply experience you do not yet have.
insight: Clear, honest level-setting builds recruiter trust faster than inflated positioning—especially in regulated healthcare hiring.

recommended_overrides.seniority_tone: Use graduate-ready, evidence-backed language that emphasizes capability to learn quickly in supervised lab environments.
recommended_overrides.experience_framing: Translate retail experience into transferable strengths (accuracy, consistency, shift reliability, customer communication) without overstating lab exposure.

title: Formatting & Bullet Style
finding: The CV uses telegraphic fragments and gerund-led bullets (e.g., "Helping customers find products", "Garden section mostly") instead of standard action-result bullet construction. Tone findings also flag mixed tense and informal phrasing.
examples: "sometimes worked in the deli when they needed people"
recommendation: Rewrite bullets in past-tense action-verb format with specific task context (and outcomes where possible), and remove conversational phrasing.
insight: Hiring teams infer professionalism from bullet mechanics before they evaluate potential.

recommended_overrides.bullet_style: Use concise, past-tense action-led bullets (Verb + task + context/outcome).
recommended_overrides.tense_consistency: Keep all prior roles in consistent past tense; avoid gerund-led fragments.
recommended_overrides.first_person: Do not use conversational or diary-style phrasing in CV bullets.

title: Linguistic Strength
finding: Several statements are flagged as weak or non-credible professional language (e.g., "Good at following instructions", "Team player", "Reliable"). These read as unsubstantiated clichés and dilute stronger evidence you do have.
recommendation: Replace generic traits with evidence-backed claims tied to real responsibilities (accuracy, handling busy shifts, cross-department support, tenure consistency).
insight: Specific evidence is persuasive; generic adjectives are usually ignored by recruiters and ATS screeners.

recommended_overrides.language_precision: Remove clichés and replace with concrete, verifiable capability statements.
recommended_overrides.evidence_density: Every key strength should be tied to an example, duration, scope, or measurable context.
recommended_overrides.professional_register: Use formal, healthcare-appropriate wording across all sections.

title: Cover Letter Style
finding: The cover letter includes self-undermining and overly casual lines that can pre-empt rejection in a clinical application (e.g., "I know I probably don't have as much experience...", "I never call in sick unless I actually am").
examples: "I know I probably don't have as much experience as other people applying but I am a quick learner..."
"I never call in sick unless I actually am"
recommendation: Shift to a confident, evidence-led graduate narrative: relevant degree foundation, lab practical exposure from university, reliability from sustained shift work, and motivation to train into clinical workflows.
insight: Cover-letter tone sets first-impression credibility—especially when direct experience is limited.

recommended_overrides.cover_letter_voice: Use confident, non-defensive language that highlights readiness and professionalism.
recommended_overrides.hedging_removal: Remove apologetic or comparative statements that position the candidate as less suitable.
recommended_overrides.value_proposition: Lead with degree relevance, lab fundamentals, and transferable reliability rather than personal reassurance statements.

title: Professional Credibility Signals
finding: A few presentation details weaken professional perception before skills are reviewed (e.g., personal-style email handle and listing an expired First Aid certificate).
recommendation: Use a professional email format and remove lapsed credentials until renewed.
insight: Small admin signals can materially affect perceived polish in high-compliance sectors like healthcare.

recommended_overrides.contact_professionalism: Use a clean professional email address format (first.last domain).
recommended_overrides.credential_hygiene: Do not list expired certifications; re-add only once current.
recommended_overrides.document_polish: Apply a compliance-oriented presentation standard across contact and credentials sections.
